correctness.rationale: For each m>=1 the exact convex hull equals the leaf-coordinate region sum max(u_i,v_i)<=1 with 2m+2^m verified irredundant facets. Projection into the two zero-sum blocks gives lower length sqrt(m/(m+1)) and upper length sqrt((m+2s(m-s))/(m+1)); the balanced s maximizes the latter. Symmetry averaging gives a globally valid upper bound and an explicit feasible center attains the intersection radius. Equality for every balanced upper facet forces all leaf coordinates and proves uniqueness; contact counts and asymptotic follow. Full numerical LP and vertex-derived hull checks for m<=12 and m<=4 respectively are supportive finite tests, not the infinite proof. No unproved auxiliary lemma or missing numerical certificate is needed.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite PQ-type graph-polytope family, obtains the exact Euclidean inradius, proves global uniqueness of the largest-ball center, and completely classifies an exponential family of facet contacts using balanced selections and parity. In contrast to established forest-normalized volume which depends only on edge count, this is an exact and genuinely metric geometric invariant; the contact proportion decays like m^(-1/2), demonstrating a nontrivial concentration pattern rather than a routine small computation.
